chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding the thief: 'When he steals, I cut off his right hand; and when he steals a second time, I cut off his left leg. Then if he steals a third time, I imprison him and leave his right leg so he may walk upon it to the latrine, and his left hand so he may eat with it and clean himself (from the latrine) with it.'
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'I am shy of Allah that I would leave him unable to benefit from anything, but rather I imprison him until he dies in prison.'
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not cut off (any further limbs) from a thief after (cutting) his hand and his leg.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the progressive punishment for a repeat thief in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi details the progressive penal code for repeat theft, establishing a jurisprudential precedent where the third offense results in imprisonment (sajn) with limited mobility rather than further amputation, ensuring the offender retains basic functions like eating and using the latrine. It highlights the practical wisdom of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) by linking this method to the practice of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (peace be upon him) and clarifying that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) did not impose penalties beyond the initial hand and leg cutting, emphasizing proportionality and mercy within the hadd framework.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, altogether from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding the thief: ‘When he steals, cut off his right hand, and when he steals again, cut off his left leg.
Then if he were to steal again, imprison him and leave his right leg to walk upon it to the WC, and his left hand, he can eat with it, and wash himself (from the WC) with it’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> am embarassed from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> that I<sup>asws</sup> would leave him not being able to do anything, but I<sup>asws</sup> would imprison him until he dies in the prison’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> did not cut (anymore) from a thief after (having cut) his hand and his leg’.
